problem_statement: Return True exactly when n is prime, otherwise False. A prime is an integer greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors: 1 and itself. n is any Python integer, excluding bool.
valid_input_domain: Return True exactly when n is prime, otherwise False. A prime is an integer greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors: 1 and itself. n is any Python integer, excluding bool.
bug_explanation: The lower-bound check allows 1 through; the divisor loop does not run, so 1 is incorrectly called prime.
provenance: Custom pilot example, drafted with AI assistance. Not copied from a benchmark; no novelty claim.

human_review_record.notes: Specification, reference solution, faulty solution and named counterexample verified. Bug confirmed: guard changed from n<2 to n<1 lets n=1 through; divisor loop does not run for n=1, so function incorrectly returns True. n=0 correctly rejected because 0<1 is true. Counterexample one (n=1) discussed.
